claim: Classical Muslim hadith scholarship explicitly treats isnad and narrator trustworthiness as part of report evaluation.
evidence: Sahih Muslim's introduction contains sections on the chain of transmission and trustworthy narrators.
The introduction also contains material on identifying defects in transmitters.
A separate methodological overview describes narrator evaluation and attention to wording differences.
contrary_or_limitations: The existence of a classical criticism method does not establish that every transmitted hadith is authentic.
A classical grading and the project's historical score are deliberately separate fields.
